items.item_text: Copy of Driver's License
Any combination equivalent to a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution in statistics, mathematics, economics, education, applied research, social sciences, or a closely related field.
Master's degree in a related field from an accredited institution.

Five (5) years of progressively responsible institutional research, institutional effectiveness, planning, assessment, or closely related experience, including experience providing lead direction, project leadership, or supervision.
Experience conducting institutional research or data analysis within the California Community Colleges.
Supervisory or lead experience in a reasonably related assignment.
Assist the Executive Director in planning, organizing, directing, and coordinating the operations of the Office of Institutional Effectiveness.
Serves as the designated administrator in the absence of the Executive Director as assigned.

In coordination with the Executive Director, provide leadership, supervision, and operational oversight for assigned functions of the Office of Institutional Effectiveness, including institutional research, strategic planning, accreditation support, data governance, institutional effectiveness, and other collegewide initiatives.
Develop, analyze, interpret, and communicate quantitative and qualitative data related to student outcomes, enrollment, workforce trends, institutional performance, and operational effectiveness.

Develop analytical reports, dashboards, scorecards, data visualizations, and presentations for executive leadership, governance committees, the Board of Trustees, external agencies, and other stakeholders.
Coordinate institutional surveys, climate assessments, research studies, and other assessment activities.
Support data governance initiatives by promoting data quality, integrity, consistency, documentation, and the appropriate use of institutional data.
Provide consultation and technical expertise to faculty, staff, and administrators on institutional research methods, data interpretation, performance metrics, and evidence-based decision-making.
Coordinate responses to internal and external requests for institutional data, research, and reporting.
Assist in preparing and submitting state, federal, accreditation, grant, and other required institutional reports.
Research and communicate emerging trends, best practices, legislation, and policy developments affecting community colleges, institutional effectiveness, and student success.
Develop and maintain office documentation, business processes, data standards, procedures, and operating guidelines.

Plan, organize, coordinate, assign, and review the work of assigned staff and student employees. Represent the Office of Institutional Effectiveness on College, District, and external committees, workgroups, and professional organizations as assigned.
Perform related duties as assigned.
Demonstrated proficiency in utilizing computer applications, including statistical analysis, statistical software, and database software.
Mission of the California Community Colleges and community college programs.
Work effectively and collaboratively with diverse faculty, staff, students, and community members.
Federal, state, and local laws, regulations, codes, and procedures related to research and institutional effectiveness.
Plan, conduct, and participate in analytical studies using research methodologies in an educational setting.
Administrative principles and practices, including goal setting, program development, implementation, and evaluation.
Plan, organize, direct, and coordinate the work of professional and technical staff, including delegating responsibilities.

Principles and methods of research design, evaluation, data collection, analysis, interpretation, and reporting used to assess institutional effectiveness, strategic planning, and key performance indicators.

Provide administrative and professional leadership for assigned institutional effectiveness functions and initiatives. Assist in developing, monitoring, and administering assigned budgets and resources.
Research methodology and statistical procedures, including sampling, correlation analysis, projections, and other quantitative and qualitative methods used in education and social research.
Learn and apply emerging technologies to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
Database design and related software applications used for research, analysis, and reporting.
Prepare comprehensive reports, presentations, and other professional documents.
ACCJC Accreditation Standards, self-evaluation report processes, and California Community Colleges Chancellor's Office reporting metrics.
Interpret and apply applicable laws, regulations, policies, procedures, and reporting requirements within assigned areas of responsibility. Manage multiple priorities and meet established deadlines.
Principles and practices of employee supervision, including work planning, assignment, review, evaluation, and training.
Train, supervise, and evaluate assigned staff and student employees.
Methods and techniques for presentations, business correspondence, information distribution, research, and reporting.
Establish and maintain positive, collaborative working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Administrative practices, and organizational and management methods used to evaluate projects, programs, policies, procedures, and operational needs.

Analyze complex issues and apply applicable institutional policies, regulatory requirements, research standards, and reporting requirements appropriately. Demonstrate cultural competency, equity-minded practices, and a commitment to serving historically minoritized populations through ongoing professional development.
Completed Online Application
Current resume
Letter of interest (Cover Letter)
Copy of legible transcripts
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, ethnic, and disability backgrounds of community college students and employees.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.
